the isolation of eleven chemical compounds from the bark of Calophyllibum inophyllum and C. soulattri, and their cytotoxic activities against four cancer cell lines.
the isolation and identification of eleven xanthone derivatives and the comparative prediction of their structure-activity relationships.
the structure-activity relationships between the xanthones and the four cancer cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a hydroxyl group at C-3 and a methoxyl group at C7 of a xanthone is important for its antiproliferation activity.
the presence of the 4,5-dihydroxyl group in the xanthone ring system is the most important structural requirement for antiproliferation.
the xanthones are a class of chemical compounds with the potential to be developed into anticancer agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the xanthones with a hydroxyl group at C4 and C8 were found to be the best antiproliferatives.
the xanthone skeleton was not the main factor for antiproliferation activity but the substituent on the xanthone core was.
compounds 1, 3, 6, 7, 9 and 10 were found to be active against all the cancer cell line tested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a hydroxyl group at position 4 of the xanthone nucleus is essential for cytotoxicity against cancer cells.
the xanthones with an α,β-unsaturated lactone moiety were found to be the best inhibitors of the cancer cells.
compounds 1-11 are potential candidates for the treatment of cancer.
